description: The Indian peafowl (Pavo cristatus), also known as the common peafowl, or blue peafowl, is a species of peafowl native to the Indian subcontinent. While it originated in the Indian subcontinent, it has since been introduced to many other parts of the world.
habitat: Deciduous forests, scrub jungles, agricultural plains, and village edges.
diet: Omnivorous — seeds, insects, small reptiles, berries, and grains.
physical_characteristics: National bird of India. Males boast iridescent blue necks with an elaborate train of eye-spotted tail covert feathers up to 2 meters long.
geographical_distribution: Throughout the Indian Subcontinent south of the Himalayas.

description: The Indian roller (Coracias benghalensis) is a bird of the family Coraciidae. It is 30–34 cm (12–13 in) long with a wingspan of 65–74 cm (26–29 in) and weighs 166–176 g (5.9–6.2 oz).
habitat: Open grasslands, agricultural cultivated fields, roadside trees, and dry deciduous scrub.
diet: Carnivorous — primarily ground beetles, crickets, grasshoppers, moths, and small frogs.
physical_characteristics: State bird of multiple Indian states. Renowned for its breathtaking turquoise and dark ultramarine blue wing patterns displayed during aerobatic courtship flights.
geographical_distribution: Widespread resident across mainland India.

description: The great Indian bustard (Ardeotis nigriceps) or Indian bustard is a bustard occurring on the Indian subcontinent. It is a large bird with a horizontal body, long bare legs and is among the heaviest of the flying birds.
habitat: Arid and semi-arid grasslands, shrublands, and desert fringes.
diet: Omnivorous — grass seeds, insects, beetles, locusts, lizards, and small snakes.
physical_characteristics: One of the heaviest flying birds on Earth (up to 15 kg). Tall, ostrich-like stance with a black crown on its head and pale neck.
geographical_distribution: Severely fragmented; primarily found in the Thar Desert (Rajasthan) and Kutch (Gujarat).

description: The house sparrow (Passer domesticus) is a bird of the sparrow family Passeridae, found in most parts of the world. It is a small bird that has a typical length of 16 cm (6.3 in) and a mass of 24–39.5 g (0.85–1.39 oz).
habitat: Urban landscapes, rural villages, farms, and suburban gardens.
diet: Granivorous & insectivorous — seeds, grains, table crumbs, and caterpillars for chicks.
physical_characteristics: Compact passerine bird. Males feature a rich chestnut brown back, grey crown, and bold black throat bib.
geographical_distribution: Ubiquitous across India and introduced worldwide.

description: The Asian Koel is a bird species found in the Indian subcontinent.
habitat: Light woodlands, gardens, cultivated orchards, and leafy city parks.
diet: Frugivorous & omnivorous — wild figs, papayas, berries, and insect larvae.
physical_characteristics: Brood parasite known for its loud 'koo-ooo' call. Males are glossy blue-black with ruby-red eyes; females are speckled and barred brown.
geographical_distribution: All Indian states and across South Asia.

description: The Rose-ringed Parakeet is a bird species found in the Indian subcontinent.
habitat: Woodlands, farmlands, gardens, urban parks, and temple groves.
diet: Herbivorous — seeds, grain, fruits, berries, and nectar.
physical_characteristics: Bright emerald green plumage with a very long graduated tail. Adult males show a distinctive rose-pink and black neck ring.
geographical_distribution: Abundant throughout India.

description: The Red-vented Bulbul is a bird species found in the Indian subcontinent.
habitat: Secondary scrub, gardens, open forests, hedges, and city foliage.
diet: Frugivorous & insectivorous — soft fruits, berries, flower nectar, and flying insects.
physical_characteristics: Dark crest on black head with scale-like pattern on chest, and an unmistakable bright crimson-red undertail patch (vent).
geographical_distribution: Native to entire Indian subcontinent.

description: The Indian Robin is a bird species found in the Indian subcontinent.
habitat: Dry open stony scrublands, agricultural borders, rocky outcrops, and village edges.
diet: Insectivorous — termites, ants, beetles, spiders, and insect pupae.
physical_characteristics: Small songbird that perches with its tail cocked upright. Males are glossy black with a white shoulder patch and chestnut-brown undertail coverts.
geographical_distribution: Endemic to the Indian Subcontinent.

description: The Jungle Babbler is a bird species found in the Indian subcontinent.
habitat: Deciduous forest, dry scrub, gardens, orchards, and thorn groves.
diet: Omnivorous — insects, spiders, grain, nectar, and fallen seeds.
physical_characteristics: Popularly nicknamed 'Seven Sisters' because they always forage in noisy, social family groups of six to ten individuals.
geographical_distribution: Common resident throughout the Indian Peninsula.

description: The Common Myna is a bird species found in the Indian subcontinent.
habitat: Human settlements, agricultural fields, pastures, and city centers.
diet: Omnivorous — insects, fruit, scraps, grains, and earthworms.
physical_characteristics: Medium brown bird with a black hooded head, yellow eye patches, bright yellow bill and legs, and white wing patches visible in flight.
geographical_distribution: Ubiquitous throughout India.

description: The Brahminy Kite is a bird species found in the Indian subcontinent.
habitat: Coastlines, rivers, lakes, flooded estuaries
physical_characteristics: Distinctive morphological characteristics of the Accipitridae family.
geographical_distribution: Broadly distributed across favorable habitats in India.

description: The Black Kite is a bird species found in the Indian subcontinent.
habitat: Urban cities, garbage dumps, lakes, fields
physical_characteristics: Distinctive morphological characteristics of the Accipitridae family.
geographical_distribution: Broadly distributed across favorable habitats in India.

description: The Shikra is a bird species found in the Indian subcontinent.
habitat: Open forests, savanna, agricultural groves
physical_characteristics: Distinctive morphological characteristics of the Accipitridae family.
geographical_distribution: Broadly distributed across favorable habitats in India.

description: The white-throated kingfisher (Halcyon smyrnensis) also known as the white-breasted kingfisher is a tree kingfisher, widely distributed in Asia from the Sinai east through the Indian subcontinent to China and Indonesia. This kingfisher is a resident over much of its range, although some populations may make short distance movements.
habitat: Wetlands, paddy fields, irrigation canals, dry plains
physical_characteristics: Distinctive morphological characteristics of the Alcedinidae family.
geographical_distribution: Broadly distributed across favorable habitats in India.

description: The Common Kingfisher is a bird species found in the Indian subcontinent.
habitat: Clear streams, rivers, ponds, reed beds
physical_characteristics: Distinctive morphological characteristics of the Alcedinidae family.
geographical_distribution: Broadly distributed across favorable habitats in India.

description: The pied kingfisher (Ceryle rudis) is a species of water kingfisher widely distributed across Africa and Asia. Originally described by Carl Linnaeus in 1758, it has five recognised subspecies, and is the only member of the genus Ceryle.
habitat: Lakes, estuaries, large rivers, reservoirs
diet: Piscivore - fish, hovers mid-air before diving
physical_characteristics: Distinctive morphological characteristics of the Alcedinidae family.
geographical_distribution: Broadly distributed across favorable habitats in India.

description: The bee-eaters are a group of birds in the family Meropidae, containing three genera and thirty-one species. Most species are found in Africa and Asia, with a few in southern Europe, Australia, and New Guinea.
habitat: Grasslands, farmlands, dry scrub, open country
physical_characteristics: Distinctive morphological characteristics of the Meropidae family.
geographical_distribution: Broadly distributed across favorable habitats in India.

description: The Indian golden oriole (Oriolus kundoo) is a species of oriole found in the Indian subcontinent and Central Asia. The species was formerly considered to be a subspecies of the Eurasian golden oriole, but is now considered a full species.
habitat: Deciduous canopy, mango orchards, tree groves
physical_characteristics: Distinctive morphological characteristics of the Oriolidae family.
geographical_distribution: Broadly distributed across favorable habitats in India.

description: The  black drongo (Dicrurus macrocercus) is a small Asian passerine bird of the drongo family Dicruridae. It is a common resident breeder in much of tropical southern Asia from southwest Iran through Pakistan, India, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka east to southern China and Indonesia and accidental visitor of Japan.
habitat: Open agricultural fields, scrublands, wire perches
physical_characteristics: Distinctive morphological characteristics of the Dicruridae family.
geographical_distribution: Broadly distributed across favorable habitats in India.

description: The ashy drongo (Dicrurus leucophaeus) is a species of bird in the drongo family Dicruridae. It is found widely distributed across eastern and Southeast Asia, with several populations that vary in the shade of grey, migration patterns and in the size or presence of white patches around the eye.
habitat: Hill forests, bamboo stands, plantation edges
diet: Insectivore - flying insects captured in air
physical_characteristics: Distinctive morphological characteristics of the Dicruridae family.
geographical_distribution: Broadly distributed across favorable habitats in India.

description: The greater coucal or crow pheasant (Centropus sinensis), is a large non-parasitic member of the cuckoo order of birds, the Cuculiformes. A widespread resident in the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia, it is divided into several subspecies, some being treated as full species.
habitat: Dense scrub, hedges, tall grassland marshes
physical_characteristics: Distinctive morphological characteristics of the Cuculidae family.
geographical_distribution: Broadly distributed across favorable habitats in India.

description: The sarus crane (Antigone antigone) is a large nonmigratory crane found in parts of the Indian subcontinent, Southeast Asia, and northern Australia. The tallest of the flying birds, standing at a height of up to 1.8 m (5 ft 11 in), they are a conspicuous species of open wetlands in South Asia, seasonally flooded Dipterocarpus forests in Southeast Asia, and Eucalyptus-dominated woodlands and grasslands in Australia.
habitat: Wetlands, flooded marshes, agricultural paddy lands
diet: Omnivore - tubers, seeds, aquatic frogs, snails
physical_characteristics: Distinctive morphological characteristics of the Gruidae family.
geographical_distribution: Broadly distributed across favorable habitats in India.

description: The painted stork (Mycteria leucocephala) is a large wader  in the stork family. It is found in the wetlands of the plains of tropical Asia south of the Himalayas in the Indian subcontinent and extending into Southeast Asia.
habitat: Shallow freshwater wetlands, marshes, reservoirs
physical_characteristics: Distinctive morphological characteristics of the Ciconiidae family.
geographical_distribution: Broadly distributed across favorable habitats in India.

description: The Asian Openbill is a bird species found in the Indian subcontinent.
habitat: Freshwater lakes, seasonal floodplains, marshes
physical_characteristics: Distinctive morphological characteristics of the Ciconiidae family.
geographical_distribution: Broadly distributed across favorable habitats in India.

description: The black-headed ibis (Threskiornis melanocephalus), also known as the Oriental white ibis, Indian white ibis, and black-necked ibis, is a species of wading bird of the ibis family Threskiornithidae which breeds in the South and Southeast Asia from India to the west and as far east as Japan. It is the only native ibis species in its range that has an overall white plumage with a black neck and head.
habitat: Inland wetlands, tidal mudflats, flooded paddy
physical_characteristics: Distinctive morphological characteristics of the Threskiornithidae family.
geographical_distribution: Broadly distributed across favorable habitats in India.

description: The red-wattled lapwing (Vanellus indicus) is an Asian lapwing or large plover, a wader in the family Charadriidae. Like other lapwings they are ground birds that are incapable of perching.
habitat: Plains near water, dry stream beds, pastures
physical_characteristics: Distinctive morphological characteristics of the Charadriidae family.
geographical_distribution: Broadly distributed across favorable habitats in India.

description: The white-breasted waterhen (Amaurornis phoenicurus) is a waterbird of the rail and crake family, Rallidae, that is widely distributed across South and Southeast Asia. They are dark slaty birds with a clean white face, breast and belly.
habitat: Marshes, ponds, ditches, dense reed thickets
diet: Omnivore - shoots, seeds, insects, small mollusks
physical_characteristics: Distinctive morphological characteristics of the Rallidae family.
geographical_distribution: Broadly distributed across favorable habitats in India.

description: The common moorhen (Gallinula chloropus), also known as the waterhen, is a bird species in the rail family (Rallidae). It is distributed across many parts of the Old World, across Africa, Europe, and Asia.
habitat: Vegetated lakes, marshy ponds, slow rivers
diet: Omnivore - aquatic vegetation, seeds, water bugs
physical_characteristics: Distinctive morphological characteristics of the Rallidae family.
geographical_distribution: Broadly distributed across favorable habitats in India.

description: The purple sunbird (Cinnyris asiaticus) is a small bird in the sunbird family. It occurs in parts of the Arabian peninsula and South and Southeast Asia.
habitat: Gardens, open scrub, flowering groves, parks
physical_characteristics: Distinctive morphological characteristics of the Nectariniidae family.
geographical_distribution: Broadly distributed across favorable habitats in India.

description: The crimson sunbird (Aethopyga siparaja) is a species of bird in the sunbird family which feed largely on nectar. They may also take insects, especially when feeding their young.
habitat: Himalayan foothills, evergreen forests, gardens
physical_characteristics: Distinctive morphological characteristics of the Nectariniidae family.
geographical_distribution: Broadly distributed across favorable habitats in India.

description: The baya weaver (Ploceus philippinus) is a weaverbird found across the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia. Flocks are found in grasslands, cultivated areas, scrub and secondary growth.
habitat: Grasslands, thorn trees near water, crop fields
physical_characteristics: Distinctive morphological characteristics of the Ploceidae family.
geographical_distribution: Broadly distributed across favorable habitats in India.

description: The Indian silverbill or white-throated munia (Euodice malabarica) is a small passerine bird found in the Indian subcontinent and adjoining regions that was formerly considered to include the closely related African silverbill (Euodice cantans). This estrildid finch is a common resident breeding bird in the drier regions of the Middle East and the Indian subcontinent.
habitat: Dry scrub, thorn bushes, savannah grasslands
physical_characteristics: Distinctive morphological characteristics of the Estrildidae family.
geographical_distribution: Broadly distributed across favorable habitats in India.

description: The scaly-breasted munia or spotted munia (Lonchura punctulata), known in the pet trade as nutmeg mannikin or spice finch, is a sparrow-sized estrildid finch native to tropical Asia. A species of the genus Lonchura, it was formally described and named by Carl Linnaeus in 1758.
habitat: Paddy fields, grasslands, secondary scrub
physical_characteristics: Distinctive morphological characteristics of the Estrildidae family.
geographical_distribution: Broadly distributed across favorable habitats in India.

description: The plum-headed parakeet (Psittacula cyanocephala) is a species of parakeet in the family Psittacidae. It is endemic to the Indian subcontinent and was once thought to be conspecific with the blossom-headed parakeet (P. roseata) before being elevated to a full species.
habitat: Moist deciduous forests, wooded valleys, fruit trees
physical_characteristics: Distinctive morphological characteristics of the Psittaculidae family.
geographical_distribution: Broadly distributed across favorable habitats in India.

description: The Alexandrine parakeet (Psittacula eupatria), also known as the Alexandrine parrot, is a medium-sized parrot in the genus Psittacula of the family Psittaculidae, native to South Asia and Southeast Asia. It is named after Alexander the Great, who transported numerous birds from Punjab to various European and Mediterranean countries and regions, where they were prized by the royalty, nobility and warlords.
habitat: Old-growth forests, plantations, tree groves
physical_characteristics: Distinctive morphological characteristics of the Psittaculidae family.
geographical_distribution: Broadly distributed across favorable habitats in India.

description: The spotted owlet (Athene brama) is a small owl which breeds in tropical Asia from North Pakistan to Southeast Asia. A common resident of open habitats including farmland and human habitation, it has adapted to living in cities.
habitat: Open country, village groves, tree hollows, ruins
physical_characteristics: Distinctive morphological characteristics of the Strigidae family.
geographical_distribution: Broadly distributed across favorable habitats in India.

description: The Barn Owl is a bird species found in the Indian subcontinent.
habitat: Old buildings, church spires, barns, rural ruins
diet: Carnivore - rats, mice, shrews, small birds
physical_characteristics: Distinctive morphological characteristics of the Tytonidae family.
geographical_distribution: Broadly distributed across favorable habitats in India.

description: The Indian eagle-owl (Bubo bengalensis), or the Bengal eagle-owl or rock eagle-owl, is a large horned owl species native to hilly and rocky scrub forests in the Indian subcontinent. It is splashed with brown and grey, and has a white throat patch with black small stripes.
habitat: Rocky ravines, arid scrub, ancient quarry walls
physical_characteristics: Distinctive morphological characteristics of the Strigidae family.
geographical_distribution: Broadly distributed across favorable habitats in India.

description: The brown fish owl (Ketupa zeylonensis) is a fish owl species in the family known as typical owls, Strigidae. It is native from Turkey to South and Southeast Asia.
habitat: Wooded streams, freshwater lakes, canal banks
physical_characteristics: Distinctive morphological characteristics of the Strigidae family.
geographical_distribution: Broadly distributed across favorable habitats in India.

description: The jungle owlet (Glaucidium radiatum) or barred jungle owlet is native to the Indian Subcontinent. The species is often found singly, in pairs or small groups, and they are usually detected by their calls at dawn and dusk.
habitat: Moist and dry deciduous forests, teak plantations
physical_characteristics: Distinctive morphological characteristics of the Strigidae family.
geographical_distribution: Broadly distributed across favorable habitats in India.

description: The coppersmith barbet (Psilopogon haemacephalus), also called crimson-breasted barbet and coppersmith, is an Asian barbet with crimson forehead and throat, known for its metronomic call that sounds similar to a coppersmith striking metal with a hammer. It is a resident bird in the Indian subcontinent and parts of Southeast Asia.
habitat: Gardens, groves, open woodlands, ficus trees
diet: Frugivore - wild figs, berries, flower petals
physical_characteristics: Distinctive morphological characteristics of the Megalaimidae family.
geographical_distribution: Broadly distributed across favorable habitats in India.

description:
The brown-headed barbet (Psilopogon zeylanicus) is an Asian barbet species native to the Indian subcontinent, where it inhabits tropical and subtropical moist broadleaf forests.


== Taxonomy ==
The brown-headed barbet was formally described in 1788 by the German naturalist Johann Friedrich Gmelin in his revised and expanded edition of Carl Linnaeus's Systema Naturae.
habitat: Forest fringes, city parks, fruit orchards
physical_characteristics: Distinctive morphological characteristics of the Megalaimidae family.
geographical_distribution: Broadly distributed across favorable habitats in India.

description: The lineated barbet (Psilopogon lineatus) is an Asian barbet native to the Terai, the Brahmaputra basin to Southeast Asia. It is a frugivore and nests in holes of tree trunks.
habitat: Dense deciduous forests, Himalayan foothills
physical_characteristics: Distinctive morphological characteristics of the Megalaimidae family.
geographical_distribution: Broadly distributed across favorable habitats in India.

description: The Indian gray hornbill (Ocyceros birostris) is a common hornbill found on the Indian subcontinent. It is mostly arboreal and is commonly sighted in pairs.
habitat: Deciduous plains, avenue trees, gardens
physical_characteristics: Distinctive morphological characteristics of the Bucerotidae family.
geographical_distribution: Broadly distributed across favorable habitats in India.

description: The Malabar pied hornbill (Anthracoceros coronatus), also known as the lesser pied hornbill, is a bird in the hornbill family, a family of tropical birds found in the Old World. The Malabar pied hornbill is a large hornbill, measuring 65 cm (26 in) in length.
habitat: Riverine evergreen forests, moist deciduous woods
diet: Frugivore - forest canopy fruits, small vertebrates
physical_characteristics: Distinctive morphological characteristics of the Bucerotidae family.

description: The common tailorbird (Orthotomus sutorius) is a songbird found across tropical and subtropical Asia. Popular for its nest made of leaves "sewn" together and immortalized by Rudyard Kipling as Darzee in his Jungle Book, it is a common resident in urban gardens.
habitat: Gardens, hedgerows, scrub, urban greenery

description: The ashy prinia or ashy wren-warbler (Prinia socialis) is a small warbler in the family Cisticolidae. This prinia is a resident breeder in the Indian subcontinent, ranging across most of India, Nepal, Bangladesh, eastern Pakistan, Bhutan, Sri Lanka and western Myanmar.

description: The plain prinia (Prinia inornata), also known as the plain wren-warbler or white-browed wren-warbler, is a small cisticolid warbler found in Southeast Asia. It is a resident breeder from Pakistan and India to south China and southeast Asia.
habitat: Paddy fields, reed beds, open marshy scrub
physical_characteristics: Distinctive morphological characteristics of the Cisticolidae family.

description: The Oriental magpie-robin (Copsychus saularis) is a small passerine bird that was formerly classed as a member of the thrush family Turdidae, but now considered an Old World flycatcher. habitat: Gardens, open broadleaf forest, cultivated lands
physical_characteristics: Distinctive morphological characteristics of the Muscicapidae family.
